footer.tagline: Encoding, conversion, cheat sheets and image tools gathered in one place — open and use.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q-account: Do the tools need an account or a fee?
faq.a-account: Neither. Open a page and use it — no sign-up, no plan, no usage limit.
faq.q-privacy: Is the data I paste uploaded?
faq.a-privacy: No. Text, images and secrets are processed on this device and the site sends no requests. The one exception is an AI provider you configure yourself — that traffic goes straight to the endpoint you set.
faq.q-mobile: Does it work on a phone?
faq.a-mobile: Yes. Phone, tablet and desktop each get their own layout; favourites and recent tools stay on this device and do not follow you to another one.
faq.q-contribute: Want a new tool, or found a bug?
faq.a-contribute: Open an issue on GitHub, or add it yourself following the guide in the repo — the whole site is MIT licensed.

ai.entryHint: When off, the polish and proofreading entries are hidden and Import PDF is greyed out. When on, content goes straight to the provider you configure here.

config.title: AI provider settings
config.pickHint: Configure several providers; pick one to edit it here.
config.notice: The key stays in this browser local storage and requests go straight from your browser to the address you set. This site neither proxies nor stores it.
config.keyPublicHint: Your key is kept in plain text in this browser's local storage. Don't paste it on a shared machine such as an internet cafe, and use "Clear all keys" when you are done.
config.baseUrlHint: You can point this at your own relay. Use https (http only for localhost); a wrong address means the request never lands.
config.modelPlaceholder: Type a model name, e.g. deepseek-chat
config.textHint: Each provider keeps its own text, vision, image and reverse-vision pick, so configuring one never overwrites another. The provider that actually runs is the one chosen at the top. The vision slot feeds PDF import, the reverse-vision slot feeds prompt reverse-engineering, and the image slot only applies to OpenAI / Gemini.
config.directBlocked: This provider has no CORS enabled: the browser will block the request, so both "Fetch models" and later calls fail. Use a CORS-enabled relay address instead.
config.fetchEmpty: That endpoint returned no models. Use "Type a model name" and fill it in.
config.listEmpty: Start with "Fetch models" at the top right. If that endpoint is unsupported, choose "Type a model name" and fill it in.

test.mismatch: The reply did not match what was expected
test.canvasUnavailable: This browser cannot create a canvas, so the vision check is unavailable

consent.title: Turn on AI assist?
consent.body: Once on, polishing, proofreading and PDF import send your resume content directly to the provider you configured, never through this site. Resume text is personal information; make sure you accept that.

clear.title: Clear every API key on this device?
clear.body: This wipes the provider keys stored in this browser and keeps your base URLs and chosen models. It cannot be undone; paste the keys again when you need them.
clear.done: All API keys were cleared from this browser.

tour.welcome: What would you like to look at? I can show you around.

dock.body: This is the navigation. Click a category to reveal its tools; click the same one again to close it. You can also collapse the rail against the left edge.

search.body: Search every tool here — Chinese names, English names and keywords all match. The pill in the top bar is the same entry, with its shortcut shown on it.

topNav.body: These pills up top are search, language and theme. To the right are the blog, GitHub and about links.

circuit.body: This circuit board is the whole toolset: each chip is a category. Light up a category tab on a chip to expand that group’s tools.
